reason: The image-only reading was revised against Graesse (and Maggioni for Laurence) to expand abbreviations and resolve stained or doubtful words in the reread passages, and the Laurence lines beyond the first reread band were read to establish that the Philip and Decius passage is present.
sources: Th. Graesse (ed.), Jacobi a Voragine Legenda aurea, 2nd ed. (Leipzig, 1850), cap. 117 (Laurence) p. 489, cap. 143 (Cosmas and Damian) pp. 636-638, cap. 145 (Michael) pp. 649-651, cap. 149 (Francis), caps. 161-162 (Eustace, All Saints); archive.org legendaaureavulg00jacouoft (page images pp. 489, 636-637)
G. P. Maggioni (ed.), Legenda aurea (Florence: SISMEL, 1998), text in Corpus Corporum, cap. CXIII De sancto Laurentio
text:
F-n2rx (Stams, Frg. 219, four bifolia). SOURCE-ASSISTED reading, 30 October 2026, made with Graesse 1850 at hand (and, for Laurence, Maggioni's text in Corpus Corporum). Lines reread on the native images: canvas 0 right page lines 1-20 (regions 4158,614,2392,786 and 4158,1300,2392,800); canvas 0 left page lines 1-9 (1030,589,2760,811); canvas 6 left page lines 1-7 (1450,680,2340,770) and the passages at 1450,1560,2150,640 and 1450,2880,2150,540; canvas 5 left page 1450,1600,2300,600; canvas 2 right page 4250,820,2650,600. All other lines rest on the image-only first reading. Regions are x,y,width,height in native pixels on 7360 x 4912 canvases. Expansions in ( ); [ ] lost, damaged or uncertain; (?) doubtful; *...* red. Line division is not marked; passages are given as running text.

Canvas 0 (Stams_STA_Frg_219_01r), right page, lines 1-20. Cosmas and Damian, etymology and opening:
Cosmas d(icitu)r a cosmos q(uo)d e(st) firma[forma?] u(e)l ornat(us)? u(e)l s(ecundu)m ysidor(um) cosmos grece latine d(icitu)r mund(us). Fuit en(im) forma aliis in exemplis ornat(us) [uirtutibus] bonis mund(us) ab omnib(us) uiciis. ¶ Damianus d(i)c(tu)s est a dama q(uo)da(m) bestia que humilis e(st) et mansueta. u(e)l damia(nus) d(icitu)r a dogma q(uod) e(st) doctrina et ana q(uod) e(st) sursum. u(e)l a damnu(m) q(uod) e(st) sacrificiu(m). u(e)l damianus q(ua)si d(omi)ni manus. Ip(s)e e(nim) h(ab)uit mansuetudine(m) in conu(er)sacione. doctrina(m) sup(er)na(m) docuit in p(re)dicacione. Sacrificiu(m) fuit in carnis mortificacione. d(omi)ni man(us) fuit in medicinali curacione. *De s(an)c(t)o cosma et damiano.* Cosmas et damianus gemini fr(atr)es in ciuitate egea ex religiosa matre no(m)i(n)e theodora nati sunt. Hii arte medicine [erasure] docti tanta(m) a sp(irit)u s(an)c(t)o gr(aci)am acceperunt ut omnes languores no(n) solu(m) ab ho(m)i(n)ib(us) s(ed) et iumentis curarent gratis o(mn)ia tribuentes. [Ma]trona aut(em) no(m)i(n)e palladia cu(m) o(mn)ia sua in medicis consu(m)psisset ad s(an)c(t)os [uiros?] accessit et ab eis sanitate(m) integra(m) reportauit. Tunc illa quodda(m) munus clam s(an)c(t)o damiano obtulit et cu(m) nollet accip(er)e illa eu(m) cu(m) sacramentis terribilibus adiurauit. Q(uo)d ille acquieuit recip(er)e no(n) q(ui)de(m) ductus cupiditate muneris s(ed) deuocione offerentis et ne uideret(ur) n(omen) d(omi)ni sp(er)nere p(er) q(uo)d se sic [marg. "sic"] adiuratu(m) uidebat. Hec s(an)c(tu)s cosmas ut comp(er)it p(re)cepit ne corpus eius una cu(m) corpore ip(s)i(us) poneretur. S(ed) sequenti nocte domin(us) cosme apparuit et fr(atre)m de suscepto munere excusauit. ¶ Audiens ergo fama(m) p(ro)consul lisias eos ad se accersiri fecit ...

Canvas 0, left page, lines 1-9. Michael, the mission of angels:
maxime desiderare alior(um) salute(m) ob q(uam) e(tiam) dicit ysayas Ecce ego d(omi)ne mitte me. Et angeli possunt nos iuuare p(ro) eo q(uod) uident nos s(uo) auxilio indig[ere] et malos angelos nos impugnare. Ideo q(uod) ad nos mittantur lex exigit angelice caritatis. Tercio hu(m)ane i(n)digencie. [mitt]untur? ... angeli ad inflammandu(m) affectu(m) ad amore(m) [unde] in figura huius leguntur [missi in] curru igneo. Secundo ad illuminandu(m) [marg. supplement "in/tellectu(m) ad"] cognicione(m). hoc signatu(m) e(st) apoc. x. in angelo qui habebat libru(m) apertu(m) in manu sua. Tercio ad corroborandu(m) in nobis omne imp(er)fectu(m) [usque in finem]. hoc signatu(m) est .iii. Regu(m) .xix. ubi angelus deportauit helye pane(m) subcinericiu(m) et uas aque. et comedit et bibit et ambulauit in fortitudine cibi illius usq(ue) ad monte(m) [dei oreb] ...

Canvas 6 (Stams_STA_Frg_219_04r), left page, lines 1-7, region 1450,680,2340,770. Laurence:
...passus est. S(ed) inter deciu(m) et dyoclecianu(m) fluxeru(n)t anni circit(er) .xl. et imp(er)atores .vii. fuerunt medio temp(or)e. ut tu(n)c b(ea)tus uincencius no(n) pot(er)it iuuenis extitisse. Beatus aut(em) sixt(us) s(an)c(tu)m laurenc(ium) suu(m) archidiacone(m) ordinauit. Eo temp(or)e phylippus imp(er)ator et fili(us) suus no(m)i(n)e phylipp(us) fidem xp(ist)i receperant et xp(ist)iani effecti eccl(es)iam sublimare plurimu(m) intendebant. Nec te moueat quod thesauri quos laurencius dispensauit no(n) dicuntur thesauri imperatoris sed ecclesie. quia potuit esse quod cum ip(s)is thesauris phylippi imperatoris aliquem etiam thesaurum eccl(es)ie dispensauit.

Canvas 6, left page, regions 1450,1560,2150,640 and 1450,2880,2150,540. Laurence continued (the lines between the two regions, on Decius's revolt, are summarized from the overview, not transcribed):
¶ Iste phylippus primus imperator fuit qui fidem xp(ist)i recepit. Que(m) origenes ut dicit(ur) ad fidem xp(ist)i conuertit. lic(et) alibi legatur quod b(ea)t(u)s ponci(us) eu(m) conuerterit. Regnauit aut(em) M° anno ab urbe condita. ut millesimus rome annus xp(ist)o potius qua(m) ydolis dicaretur. Qui quide(m) annus millesimus fuit a romanis cu(m) ingenti ludoru(m) (et) spectaculor(um) apparatu celebratus. Erat aut(em) phylippo imperatori miles quida(m) no(m)i(n)e decius in armis bellicis industris plurimu(m) (et) famosus. [...] ...ad urbe(m) regiam gradu concito properauit. Audiens hec phylippus iunior uehementer extimuit (et) totu(m) thesaurum patris (et) suum b(ea)t(o) syxto (et) s(an)c(t)o laurencio comendauit ut si ip(su)m a decio interfici contingeret. thesauru(m) ip(su)m ecclesiis (et) paup(er)ib(us) erogarent. ¶ Post hec phylippus aufugit (et) se a facie decii occultauit. Senat(us) ig(itur) obuia(m) [decio processit]

Canvas 5 (Stams_STA_Frg_219_03v), left page, region 1450,1600,2300,600. End of Eustace, opening of All Saints:
[pas]si sunt aut(em) sub adriano qui cep(it) circa annu(m) d(omi)ni c.xx. kal(endis) nouembr(is). u(e)l s(ecundu)m quosda(m) xii kal(endis) octobris. ¶ Omniu(m) s(an)c(t)or(um) festiuitas *De festiuitate omnium sanctorum* quatuor de causis instituta fuisse uidetur. p(ri)mo p(ro)pt(er) cuiusdam templi dedicatione(m). Sec(un)do p(ro)pt(er) obmissor(um) suppletionem. t(er)tio p(ro)pt(er) negligentiar(um) expiationem. quarto p(ro)pt(er) faciliorem orationum n(ost)rar(um) i(m)petrationem. P(ri)mo ig(itur) instituta e(st) p(ro)pt(er) templi dedicatione(m). Romani enim cum uniuerso orbi d(omi)narent(ur) quoddam templu(m) maximu(m) construxerunt in cuius medio suu(m) ydolum collocantes omniu(m) p(ro)uinciaru(m) simulachra p(er) circuitum statuerunt. respicientia rectis [uultibus]

Canvas 2 (Stams_STA_Frg_219_02r), right page, region 4250,820,2650,600. Francis, the seraph and the stigmata:
q(uonia)m ad sedem p(er) sup(er)biam p(er)ditam humilitas leuabit humilem. ¶ In uisione d(e)i seru(us) [marg. se] sup(er) seraphin crucifixum aspex(it). qui crucifixionis sue signa sic euidenter ei impressit. ut crucifixus uideretur (et) ip(s)e. consignant(ur) manus. pedes. (et) latus crucis caractere. s(ed) diligenti studio ab omniu(m) oculis ip(s)a stigmata abscondebat. ¶ Quidam tamen in uita sua uiderunt ea. s(ed) in morte plurimi conspexerunt. Quod aut(em) hec stigmata p(er) o(mn)ia uera extiterint multis miraculis est ostensum
